title: [CmdPal] Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.exe crashes ~40s after launch in RPCRT4.dll (0xc0020043); hotkey never works

judgment.rationale: The native RPC fault needs the failing exception/thread stack; Click to Do resource warnings and a similarly timed redirect timeout are not enough to assign causality. Do not ask for another reset, extension purge, exact WER code, or the already-supplied diagnostic ZIP. Obtain one exception-time dump via a private diagnostic route, then choose the responsible activation/RPC boundary.
evidence: The report supplies RPCRT4.dll 0xc0020043, fault offset, multiple WER report IDs, repeatable 35–45-second startup timing, and a diagnostic ZIP.
The author already removed third-party extensions, disabled Dock, reset LocalState, verified non-elevation/GPO, and compared 0.100.2 with 0.101.2362. None eliminated the crash.
The archive's CmdPal log has startup plus Click to Do resource lookup errors, then no managed crash stack. An earlier run reports a 32-second activation redirect timeout.

Source inspected at main 9227a8497750: src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Program.cs: RedirectActivationTo has a 32-second cancellation timeout and catches/logs cancellation and ordinary exceptions; this path is relevant context but does not prove the native RPCRT4 fault. https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/9227a8497750c257a0682b53c556d07f48ed8ff3/src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Program.cs

Downloaded the supplied report and inspected current CmdPal startup excerpts and its application event evidence. Those do not contain a native exception stack sufficient to tie the fault to resource loading.
Reviewed current Program.cs history and existing activation work; no retrieved issue-reference PR proves coverage of this signature. Product startup was not executed here.
judgment.recommended_action: Capture one exception-time CmdPal crash dump privately

fix_assessment.rationale: Qualified lightweight investigation/fix direction, not a full design. The recurring signature and control matrix establish a serious crash, but no dump or native stack connects it to a specific source branch.

proposed_fixes.title: Attribute the native CmdPal RPC crash before changing activation logic
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis only: an activation/RPC lifetime or cancellation boundary fails during startup; matching timing does not prove the 32-second redirect path or Click to Do resource warnings caused the native exception.
plan: Inspect one exception-time dump with matching module versions and identify the crashing RPC call/thread and ownership chain.
Reproduce the identified operation on a controlled same-build machine, keeping the already-cleared extensions/dock controls fixed.
Correct the confirmed lifetime/cancellation/error boundary and coordinate with existing activation changes rather than suppressing arbitrary resource errors.
verification: CmdPal survives repeated cold starts beyond the prior 45-second window and responds to its hotkey.
Single-instance redirects, timeout recovery and ordinary extension/resource failures do not terminate the owning process.

confidence.rationale: The recurring signature and control matrix establish a serious crash, but no dump or native stack connects it to a specific source branch.

comment.body: The exact RPC signature, WER IDs, timing and extensive controls are already useful—please do not repeat the reset, dock, extension, elevation or GPO tests, or re-upload the same ZIP. The missing evidence is the exception-time native thread stack. Could you capture one Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.exe crash with Windows Error Reporting LocalDumps configured for that executable (full user-mode dump / DumpType 2), then reproduce the existing 35–45-second crash once? Collection instructions: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/wer/collecting-user-mode-dumps . Dumps may contain private data: arrange a maintainer-approved private upload instead of attaching one publicly, and remove the per-app dump configuration afterward. That should distinguish activation redirection from an unrelated RPC client failure.
